extDescription.message: Blocks all traffic that doesn't go through Firefox's built-in VPN, so your real IP doesn't leak if the VPN turns off.

actionTitleOn.message: VPN Kill Switch for Firefox: on

actionTitleOff.message: VPN Kill Switch for Firefox: off

offNote.message: Pages can load without the VPN and reveal your real IP.

privateBody.message: Go to Add-ons → VPN Kill Switch for Firefox and turn on “Run in Private Windows”.

blockedHeading.message: Page blocked: the VPN isn't on

blockedLead.message: The kill switch cut the connection so your real IP isn't exposed.

blockedArt.message: The connection between the browser and the internet is cut

blockedStep1Body.message: Use the VPN button in the toolbar or in Firefox's menu.

blockedStep2Body.message: If the VPN was already on and pages are still blocked, turn it off and on once.

welcomeArt.message: Browser traffic goes through the VPN before reaching the internet

welcomeHeading.message: Firefox now browses only through its VPN

welcomeLead.message: If the VPN turns off, pauses or fails, pages won't load instead of going out with your real IP.

welcomeStep1Title.message: Turn the VPN off and on once

welcomeStep1Body.message: Only if it was already on when you installed the extension. This puts the VPN ahead of the kill switch.

welcomeStep2Title.message: Allow the extension in private windows

welcomeStep2Body.message: Go to Add-ons → VPN Kill Switch for Firefox and turn on “Run in Private Windows”. Without it, private windows aren't protected.

welcomeNote.message: To turn it off, open the extension's button and use the switch. Your local network and the services the VPN needs to connect (Mozilla accounts, vpn.mozilla.org and encrypted DNS) are never blocked.
